system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: production cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) at work
G2: production on-call
G3: cluster administration
G4: CKA certification (not yet passed)
G5: Terraform at work

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing CKA or Terraform Associate as held certifications
T2: Claiming AWS/GCP production experience or 'managed Kubernetes clusters'
T3: Presenting homelab tools (Argo CD, Prometheus, Terraform) as work experience
T4: Claiming production on-call / SRE incident ownership
T5: Retitling her current job as 'DevOps Engineer' instead of her real title
T6: Old cover letter is addressed to her current employer and says she is at Brightmill

# OUTPUT 1: CV
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | Test Infrastructure & DevOps
Professional Summary
QA automation and test-infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing GitLab CI
pipelines, Kubernetes-based ephemeral environments, infrastructure observability, and a personal
Terraform-managed VPS project. Built Kubernetes-based merge-request environments, improved
pipeline speed and cost, and developed test observability dashboards. Personal infrastructure projects
include a k3s cluster managed with GitOps and a Hetzner VPS provisioned with Terraform. AWS
experience is limited to personal learning with EC2 and S3 basics.
Core Skills
CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, pipeline profiling and optimization, dependency caching, parallel test
execution
Containers and orchestration: Docker, Kubernetes, k3s, Helm, Argo CD
Infrastructure as code and configuration: Terraform (personal project; VPS provisioning),
Ansible (basic)
Monitoring and data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Automation and testing: Java, Selenium, Python, pytest, Bash, pytest-xdist, end-to-end and
regression testing
Cloud and Infrastructure Projects: AWS EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning); Hetzner VPS
(personal project)
Professional Experience
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software 2021–Present
• Own GitLab CI pipelines and ephemeral test environments for three teams.
• Designed and implemented the delivery and lifecycle workflow for merge-request environments used
by QA and product teams for pre-merge reviews and end-to-end testing.
• Automated environment cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity; enabled QA and product
teams to review features before merge and run end-to-end tests against each environment.
• Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelized test jobs, added dependency caching and
separated end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage. Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14
minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
• Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and created Grafana dashboards to identify flaky tests by
team. Flaky test rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams addressed the leading offenders.
• Wrote the internal guide to how the CI system works; the document is used in onboarding.
• Mentored two QA interns in 2023.
• Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; the platform team operates the
cluster.
QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House 2019–2021
• Tested web and mobile applications for multiple clients.
• Introduced the first automated regression suite on the largest project, using Java and Selenium.
• Set up Jenkins to run regression tests nightly. Before automation, a full regression took two people
three days.
Selected Infrastructure Projects
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal 2024–2025
• Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster, with applications deployed from a Git repository
using Argo CD.
• Configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS certificate management; added Prometheus,
Grafana, and Loki for monitoring.
• Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform.
• Technologies: k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, Ansible (basic).
Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health 2023–2024
• Implemented short-lived merge-request environments for the application, PostgreSQL, and seeded
data on a shared Kubernetes cluster, with automated lifecycle management.
• Technologies: GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, Docker, Bash, PostgreSQL.
Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health 2023
• Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
• Flaky test rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams began fixing the most frequent offenders.
• Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API.
CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health 2022
• Optimized pipelines across three teams through parallelized test jobs, dependency caching, and a
dedicated end-to-end test stage.
• Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.
Certifications & Professional Development
• ISTQB Foundation Level, 2019
• Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA): studying; exam booked for January 2027 (not yet
passed)
• Terraform Associate: completed practice tests; certification exam not taken

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,
I’m writing to apply for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity
role. In my current role at Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines and ephemeral
test environments for three teams, working with QA and product teams to make pre-merge
review and end-to-end testing practical.
I designed and implemented short-lived merge-request environments on a shared Kubernetes
cluster, using Helm and GitLab CI to deploy the application, PostgreSQL, and seeded data,
with automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity. I have also profiled pipelines
across three teams, introducing parallel test execution, dependency caching, and a dedicated
end-to-end stage. This reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI
runner costs by about 30%. To help teams understand and improve their systems, I collected
CI results in PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards that helped reduce the flaky test rate
from 7% to below 1% after teams addressed the leading issues.
Alongside my professional work, I built a three-node k3s homelab with applications deployed
through Argo CD and provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform as a personal
infrastructure-as-code project. The homelab also used Traefik ingress and cert-manager for
TLS certificate management, with Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki providing monitoring.
These experiences have strengthened my practical understanding of infrastructure automation
and operating observable environments. I’m interested in applying that foundation to
Corvale’s work connecting a new train fleet with cloud services, and in contributing to an
engineering-led team shaping its systems from the start. I also bring a strong communication
and knowledge-sharing focus: I wrote Odrava’s internal guide to how the CI system works,
and the document is now used for onboarding. My cloud exposure also includes basic personal
learning with AWS EC2 and S3.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how
my experience in test infrastructure, infrastructure automation, observability, and technical
process improvement could contribute to Corvale’s Fleet Connectivity work.
Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
